question: During a rollout, how much do delayed, missing and corrected deployment/topology records change which Pod a pipeline attributes a request to, and does the two-clock use / fall-back / abstain policy do better than latest-state and plain temporal-join policies given identical records and the same cutoff?

rules.time_and_cutoff: t = request i's t_req (client root span start, microseconds, client clock); cutoff c = t + Delta on the same time line (Delta in {0, 5, 30, 120 s}); hindsight = every record and every correction. The request itself is known at t (attribution-lag variant V1).
rules.usable_record: a record version is usable at c iff available_at <= c and no correction of it has available_at <= c (append-only: a correction withdraws its predecessor from its own availability on; nothing is deleted or overwritten). Every policy receives exactly the usable versions at the same c.
rules.records: Pod STATE records of the two recommendationservice Pods, derived by attribution-lag-v1's pod_observations() from policy-gate-v1's load_sightings()/build_observations() (pod_state(): Failed->failed, Succeeded->succeeded, deletionTimestamp->terminating, Running with all containers ready->ready, else not_ready; absent = missing from a later complete Pods list, available when the whole list is). observed_at = host receipt of the list response; available_at = capture-era pipeline receipt. Record IDs: api/N = api:<collection 1e40730b-...>/N; absence/NNN-pods:<uid8>.
rules.latest_state: per Pod, the usable record with the greatest observed_at (then available_at, record_id) at c; t is ignored; always CONFIRMED; no lifecycle rules (they need t).
rules.temporal_join: per Pod, valid intervals [observed_at, next observed_at of that Pod) over the usable records (as-of / SCD-2 reading; a record with a recorded end uses it); the interval covering t is used (CONFIRMED); if none covers t, the nearest earlier record (FALLBACK; never happens with these sightings); no row at or before t -> the Pod is absent from the join (not serving). No abstention. Lifecycle rules K2/K1 are applied but never change an answer (checked).
rules.bitemporal_abstain: per Pod, with p = last usable sighting at or before t and n = first usable sighting after t: p and n same value -> CONFIRMED (assumption A1); a sighting exactly at t and none later -> CONFIRMED; p and n differ -> ABSTAIN transition_between_records; no p -> ABSTAIN no_record_at_or_before_t (a snapshot is not extended backwards); only p: t - p < F -> FALLBACK (carried forward), else ABSTAIN stale_beyond_freshness. F = 600 s (primary, the policy-gate audit's carry-forward) or 30 s (sensitivity).
rules.lifecycle_rules: for the two valid-time policies, before the policy: K2 creationTimestamp floor > t -> not serving; K1 last usable sighting at or before t is terminating/failed/succeeded/absent -> not serving (irreversible). Both CONFIRMED. Same order as attribution-lag's classify_pod.
rules.serving: S0: a Pod serves at t iff its state at t is ready (routing assumption, as in attribution-lag).
rules.attribution: exactly one Pod serving and no other Pod possibly serving -> that Pod (CONFIRMED if every in-view Pod's status is CONFIRMED, else FALLBACK); no Pod possibly serving -> ABSTAIN no_serving_pod_confirmed; one possibly serving but unconfirmed -> ABSTAIN serving_pod_unconfirmed; two possibly serving -> ABSTAIN two_pods_possible for bitemporal_abstain; for the non-abstaining policies two serving Pods would be broken towards the newest Pod (tie_break_newest; counted). A Pod with no usable record is not in view and not a candidate.
rules.metrics: correct / wrong against the span-verified Pod; abstain = no Pod named; harmful = wrong (a wrong instance is harmful, an abstention is not); coverage = (correct + wrong) / 120; wrong_confirmed / wrong_fallback split the wrong answers by the status the policy attached.
rules.flips: a saved answer at cutoff c flips if the same policy, re-deciding the same request on the same stream with every record and correction (hindsight), names another Pod (flip_to_other) or abstains (flip_to_abstain). resolved_later = abstained at c, answers in hindsight (not a flip). answers_using_withdrawn_version = answers at c whose records include a version later withdrawn by a correction.

bitemporal_vs_attribution_lag_rules.scope: bitemporal_abstain (F = 600 s and 30 s) with lifecycle rules K2/K1 versus experiments/attribution-lag-v1 attribute() (K2, K1, A1, S0; its F set to the same value in memory), on every perturbed stream x request x Delta; withdrawn (corrected) versions are removed before calling attribute(), which applies the availability cutoff itself

per_pod_state_vs_temporal_resolver.scope: per-Pod STATE before K1/K2, every perturbed stream x request x Delta x Pod; bitemporal_abstain (F = 600 s and 30 s) status/value versus GraphStore and SqliteStore resolve() over materialize_facts() of the versions usable at the cutoff (resolved via a known-open fact beyond its confirmation = FALLBACK; other resolved = CONFIRMED; unknown/conflict = ABSTAIN)

limitations: One rollout of one single-replica service (maxSurge 1, maxUnavailable 0) on a single-node kind cluster; no fault.
Pods were listed by polling every 2.4-3.8 s; a change inside a polling gap cannot be placed.

Request times (client clock) and API receipt times (host clock) are not calibrated against each other; creationTimestamp has 1 s resolution (API-server clock). The clock perturbations show where this matters.
Perturbations are simulated on top of measured timestamps. The measured record-delivery lag (available_at - observed_at) was sub-millisecond; delays, drops and corrections are not measured events.
The policies are simple by design (one rule each). Assumption A1 (no flap between equal sightings) and S0 (serving = ready) are modelling assumptions, as in attribution-lag-v1.

n is tiny: 120 requests from one rollout, most of them far from any transition. Apart from the 10-60 s simulated feed delays, only 5-13 requests near the switch differ between policies. Replay variants are not independent incidents. No accuracy claim.
The decision is instance attribution (which Pod served a request), not root-cause ranking; no fault, diagnosis baseline or remediation is involved.
